report.source_text: The patient was promptly initiated on immunotherapy with intravenous (IV) methylprednisolone 1000 mg daily for 5 days and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) 2 g/kg over two days. He also received one dose of IV tocilizumab 8 mg/kg 12 hours from hospital presentation. Normothermia at 35°C to 36°C was maintained for six days. Serum sodium levels were kept minimally at 140 mmol/L for neuroprotection. He received a five-day course of IV remdesivir to treat SARS-CoV-2. Other concurrent antimicrobials included empirical IV ceftriaxone, azithromycin, acyclovir, and oseltamivir, until respective viral and bacterial studies returned negative.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Acute Necrotizing Encephalitis (ANEC) associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection
clinician.trajectory_summary: An 11-year-old previously well boy, partially vaccinated with one dose of Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine one month prior, presented with two days of fever, nausea, and vomiting. SARS-CoV-2 antigen rapid test was positive at initial presentation to general practitioner and he was discharged with symptomatic management. He re-presented the next day with acute neurological deterioration including dizziness, slurred speech, left gaze deviation, progressive unsteady gait, and weakness. Neurological examination revealed reduced consciousness, expressive aphasia, bilateral partial ptosis with ophthalmoplegia, and bilateral cerebellar signs (dysdiadochokinesia, past-pointing, mild truncal ataxia). SARS-CoV-2 PCR was positive with Ct 20.49. Lumbar puncture showed elevated CSF red blood cells (25 cells/uL) and elevated protein (1.02 g/L) with normal glucose, lactate, and opening pressure; no pleocytosis; absent oligoclonal bands; and negative CSF meningoencephalitis infectious panel including negative SARS-CoV-2 PCR. Brain MRI demonstrated characteristic ANEC findings with swelling and signal changes involving bilateral thalami, midbrain, pons, cerebellar hemispheres, and periventricular white matter. The patient was promptly treated with IV methylprednisolone 1000 mg daily for 5 days, IVIG 2 g/kg over 2 days, IV tocilizumab 8 mg/kg at 12 hours from presentation, IV remdesivir for 5 days, empirical antimicrobials (ceftriaxone, azithromycin, acyclovir, oseltamivir), therapeutic hypothermia (35-36°C for 6 days), and sodium management (≥140 mmol/L). After 8 days of treatment, Glasgow Coma Scale improved to 15, ophthalmoplegia and ataxia improved, and mRS score was 2. He was discharged after 16 days with residual mild ophthalmoplegia, upper limb dysmetria with intention tremor, mild aphasia, and dysarthria (mRS 1). At two-week follow-up, mRS score improved to 0, indicating complete neurological function recovery.
